requirements.Title: Customer-Facing Improvements Must Be Clearly Defined
requirements.Description: All product requirements for the Magellan printer must be clearly defined with a focus on customer-facing improvements and visible touchpoints. Requirements should be measurable and not reference vague comparisons to predecessors.
requirements.Rationale: Ensures that improvements are tangible and meaningful to end users, driving higher satisfaction and competitive differentiation.
requirements.Dependencies: Requires input from customer insights and validation teams.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Each requirement must specify a measurable metric and be clearly linked to a customer-facing feature or experience.

requirements.Title: Insight-Driven Requirements
requirements.Description: Requirements must be based on customer insights, market research, or data-driven findings rather than assumptions or legacy practices.
requirements.Rationale: Aligns product development with real market and customer needs.
requirements.Dependencies: Access to up-to-date market research and customer feedback.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Each requirement includes a reference to supporting insight or research data.

requirements.Title: Performance and Feature Enhancements
requirements.Description: The Magellan printer must include specific performance and feature improvements, with measurable targets and thresholds for each.
requirements.Rationale: Drives product competitiveness and addresses performance gaps or opportunities.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Each performance/feature requirement includes a target (design goal) and threshold (acceptable to ship), both quantifiable.

requirements.Title: Quality Improvement and Serviceability
requirements.Description: The product must include requirements for quality improvement and enhanced serviceability, with clear metrics and service processes defined.
requirements.Rationale: Improved quality and serviceability reduce warranty costs and increase customer loyalty.
requirements.Stakeholders: Quality, Support, Service Teams, End Users
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Quality and serviceability requirements are documented with measurable KPIs and service procedures.

requirements.Title: Telemetry Integration
requirements.Description: Telemetry features must be included within the PRD scope for the Magellan printer, enabling remote monitoring and diagnostics.
requirements.Rationale: Telemetry allows proactive maintenance and improved product support.
requirements.Dependencies: Availability of telemetry infrastructure and compatible hardware.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Telemetry data can be remotely accessed and provides actionable insights for diagnostics.

requirements.Title: Documentation and Process Requirements
requirements.Description: Comprehensive documentation and process requirements must be specified, including test setup, fixtures, and process expectations for builds.
requirements.Rationale: Ensures manufacturing and support teams have clear instructions, reducing errors and delays.
requirements.Dependencies: Alignment with manufacturing and R&D documentation standards.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: All process and documentation requirements are delivered prior to relevant build phases (e.g., PP, MP).

requirements.Title: Design for Manufacturing (DFM)
requirements.Description: The Magellan printer must be designed with manufacturability in mind, following DFM guidelines such as limiting the number of colors per product and optimizing assembly processes.
requirements.Rationale: Improves production efficiency, reduces costs, and minimizes manufacturing errors.
requirements.Dependencies: DFM guideline documentation and review processes.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: DFM compliance is verified during design reviews and documented in manufacturing deliverables.

requirements.Title: Cost Reduction Initiatives
requirements.Description: Cost reduction proposals must be captured and tracked, including changes to component specifications (e.g., reducing power cord and USB cable lengths, eliminating glossy finishes).
requirements.Rationale: Supports competitive pricing and margin objectives.
requirements.Dependencies: Impact assessment and alignment with technical and regulatory constraints.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Cost reduction measures are documented, assessed, and approved without compromising product quality or compliance.

requirements.Title: Common Requirements Linkage
requirements.Description: For all common requirements (Regulatory/Safety, Environmental/Sustainability, Hardware Reliability), the PRD must reference the respective governance owner’s SharePoint documentation and revision.
requirements.Rationale: Ensures traceability and compliance with cross-product standards.
requirements.Stakeholders: Tech Reg, Product Steward, DVAR, Program Leads
requirements.Dependencies: Availability and maintenance of SharePoint documentation.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Each common requirement in the PRD includes a direct link to the latest governing document revision.

requirements.Title: Requirement Categorization and Routing
requirements.Description: Requirements outside PRD scope (not customer-facing or insight-driven) must be saved to a separate worksheet and reviewed for possible re-inclusion or routing to appropriate forums.
requirements.Rationale: Prevents loss of valuable information and ensures correct handling of all requirements.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: All out-of-scope requirements are logged and dispositioned within the program workflow.

requirements.Title: Requirement Input Structure
requirements.Description: All requirements must be entered using a standardized column structure: Priority, Target, Threshold, Justification, Requirement, SKUs Applicable, SubCategory, Category, Type, Requestor Function, Requestor Item No.
requirements.Rationale: Standardization improves traceability, review efficiency, and data integrity.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: 100% of requirements in the PRD follow the defined column structure.

requirements.Title: Measurable Thresholds and Targets
requirements.Description: Every requirement must specify a measurable threshold (minimum acceptable) and target (design goal), avoiding ambiguous language such as 'equal or better than predecessor.'
requirements.Rationale: Improves clarity, accountability, and testability of requirements.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Each requirement includes quantifiable threshold and target values.

requirements.Title: Customer-Centric Requirement Phrasing
requirements.Description: Requirements should be phrased from the customer’s perspective to ensure clarity and actionable outcomes (e.g., 'No visible tire mark' rather than vague technical comparisons).
requirements.Rationale: Enhances alignment with customer expectations and simplifies validation.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Customer-facing requirements are reviewed for clarity and phrasing from the user’s perspective.

requirements.Title: Modernize PLC with Agentic AI
requirements.Description: Integrate Agentic AI into the Product Lifecycle Control (PLC) process for design specification and test validation.
requirements.Rationale: Leverages AI to improve specification accuracy and automate test validation, increasing efficiency and reducing errors.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Agentic AI is deployed in at least one PLC phase, with measurable improvements in specification or validation accuracy.
